facts.fact: Notice of claim, municipalities and their officers or employees
facts.value: Written notice within 120 days of the event (893.80(1d)(a)). Alternatively, actual notice plus no prejudice to the defendant (893.80(1d)(a)). A claim must then be filed and disallowed before suit. Suit must be brought within 6 months of written disallowance (893.80(1g)).

facts.fact: Notice of claim, state, its agencies and employees
facts.value: Written notice to the Attorney General within 120 days. Claims proceed through the Claims Board or the courts. Notice is a condition precedent to suit.

$50,000 per claim against a municipality, its officers or employees (893.80(3)). $250,000 against the state, its officers or employees (893.82(6)). Courts have read the municipal cap narrowly, e.g. against the direct-action statute 632.24. Check Sorenson v. Batchelder, 2016 WI 34, on whether the cap applies to insurers.
